Revoking a narrow one also drops the broader permission above it — revoke delete and manage goes too, because otherwise it would still satisfy the delete check and the revoke would do nothing.
vendorAccess.overridesDescription: One row per permission, with who set it and why. Give each a reason — it is what makes the decision answerable months later — and an expiry when the access is only meant to be temporary, so nobody has to remember to take it back. A plan change never touches these.

localRetired.title: Local storage has been retired
localRetired.body: Files already on this server keep loading, but new uploads need one of the providers below. Pick one, enter its credentials, then open “Move the files you already have” — it has the commands and the backup to take before your next deploy.

cloudflare_r2.bucket: In the Cloudflare dashboard open R2 → Create bucket. Its name goes in Bucket Name above.
cloudflare_r2.token: R2 → Manage R2 API Tokens → Create API token, permission Object Read & Write, scoped to that bucket. Copy both halves into Access Key ID and Secret Access Key — the secret is shown once.
cloudflare_r2.account: Copy the 32-character Account ID from the R2 overview sidebar into R2 Account ID.
cloudflare_r2.public: Bucket → Settings → Public access: enable the r2.dev subdomain or connect a custom domain, then paste that address into Public URL.
cloudflare_r2.test: Press Test connection, then save. The test uploads a probe object and fetches it back over the public URL, so it fails if the step above was skipped.
cloudflare_r2.caution: Without a Public URL every product image returns 403 in the browser while the credentials still look correct — uploads fall back to the private R2 endpoint, which is never anonymously readable. A custom domain beats r2.dev: Cloudflare's CDN then answers cached requests without billing the bucket.

s3.bucket: Create a bucket in the S3 console and note its region — it has to match the region selected above.
s3.iam: IAM → create a user with programmatic access and a policy granting these actions on that bucket:
s3.public: Allow public reads with a bucket policy, or put CloudFront in front of the bucket, and paste the resulting address into Public URL.
s3.test: Paste the access key pair above, press Test connection, then save.
s3.caution: New buckets have Block all public access switched on. Leave it on only if you serve through CloudFront — otherwise every image on the storefront returns 403.

minio.run: Run MinIO next to the app — Coolify and Dokploy both have a one-click template. Mount a volume at /data, or the next redeploy takes every uploaded file with it.
minio.keys: Open the MinIO console (port 9001 by default), create a bucket, then Access Keys → Create access key.
minio.fields: Endpoint URL is the API address (port 9000), not the console. Region can stay us-east-1 — MinIO ignores it. Public URL is where browsers reach the bucket.
minio.caution: Serve MinIO over HTTPS on its own subdomain. Browsers block mixed content, so an http:// endpoint breaks every image on an HTTPS storefront.

digitalocean.space: Spaces Object Storage → Create a Space. The datacenter you pick is the endpoint (nyc3, fra1, sgp1…), so choose one near your shoppers and select the same region above.
digitalocean.keys: API → Spaces Keys → Generate New Key, and copy both halves into Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.
digitalocean.public: Space → Settings → set File Listing to public, or enable the CDN.
digitalocean.test: Leave Public URL blank to serve from the Space itself, or paste the CDN endpoint (…cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com) to serve from the edge. Then Test connection and save.
digitalocean.caution: The Space name is the Bucket Name above, and a Space cannot be moved between datacenters afterwards — its region is fixed when you create it.

migration.title: Move the files you already have
migration.intro: Choosing a provider only changes where new uploads go. Everything uploaded before it stays where it was and keeps loading until you move it across.
migration.step1: Configure a provider above and press Test connection — the migration uploads into whatever is saved here.
migration.step2: Move the stored credentials to the per-provider layout. Safe on any version, and a no-op once it has run.
migration.step3: Upload the local files and rewrite their URLs across the database. The dry run lists every file and writes nothing.
migration.step4: Check the storefront and the Media Library. Nothing is ever deleted from the disk, so remove the local copies by hand once the images load.
migration.backup: Before your next deploy: if your update method replaces the app folder — cPanel upload, zip overwrite, a container with no volume — copy the media off the server first. Replacing the folder deletes it.
migration.note: A file that fails to upload keeps its local URL, so a partial run leaves a working store rather than a half-broken one. Re-running is safe.

intro.title: Your AI sales agent, end to end
intro.description: The agent lives in a chat widget on your storefront. It understands what shoppers ask, looks up your real catalog and policies, recommends products, and can even add items to the cart — all using the model and rules you configure here. Follow the setup checklist below to get it live.

capabilities.title: What the agent can do
capabilities.description: Each capability you enable in Configuration unlocks one of these abilities.
capabilities.multilingualDescription: Detects and answers in the shopper's own language, whatever the storefront locale.

checklist.title: Setup checklist
checklist.description: Work through these steps to get the agent ready for shoppers. Status updates live as you configure each section.

apiKey.title: Add your OpenAI API key
apiKey.description: Set OPENAI_API_KEY in your server environment, then restart the app. The agent and its widget stay disabled until a valid key is detected.
apiKey.hint: Server-side only — the key is never exposed to shoppers.

model.title: Choose a model & runtime
model.description: Pick the model, reasoning effort, temperature, and how many products a single reply may recommend.

capabilities.title: Turn on the capabilities you want
capabilities.description: Enable product Q&A, recommendations, cart actions, checkout handoff, and order status. Each one unlocks a tool the agent is allowed to use.

identity.title: Define identity, tone & greeting
identity.description: Give the agent a name and voice, write the opening greeting, and add custom instructions for your brand and policies.

faq.title: Add FAQ knowledge
faq.description: Teach the agent your real policies (shipping, returns, sizing, warranty) so it answers from facts instead of guessing.
faq.hintWithCount: {count, plural, =0 {No FAQ entries yet} =1 {1 FAQ entry added} other {# FAQ entries added}}

widget.title: Style the widget
widget.description: Match the launcher and chat panel to your brand — colors, position, avatar, and the launcher label shoppers see.
widget.hint: Optional, but a branded widget converts better.

enableWidget.title: Enable the storefront widget
enableWidget.description: Flip the master switch so the agent appears on your storefront. Requires the OpenAI key above.

testChat.title: Test before you launch
testChat.description: Use the Test chat tab to chat exactly like a shopper would, and review real conversations once it is live.
testChat.hintWithCount: {count, plural, =0 {No conversations yet} =1 {1 conversation so far} other {# conversations so far}}

flow.title: How a conversation flows
flow.description: What happens behind the scenes every time a shopper sends a message.

open.title: Shopper opens the widget
open.body: The launcher appears on your storefront and greets them with your configured greeting message.

ask.title: They ask in their own words
ask.body: “Do you have a waterproof jacket under $100?”, “Where is my order?”, or “What is your return policy?” — no menus or keywords needed.

tools.title: The model decides which tools to use
tools.body: Based on the enabled capabilities, the agent can search your catalog, pull product details, read your FAQ, check the cart, look up order status, or add items to the cart.

data.title: It pulls live data from your store
data.body: Results come from your real, visible products and the policies you entered — so answers stay grounded instead of made up. Products render as rich cards, not plain text.

reply.title: It replies and can take action
reply.body: The shopper gets a concise answer with product cards, add-to-cart buttons, or a checkout handoff when they are ready to buy.

logged.title: Everything is logged
logged.body: Each conversation, message, and action is saved so you can review them in the Conversations tab and track performance on the Overview.

faq.title: Keep your FAQ accurate
faq.body: The agent answers policy questions from your FAQ first. Cover shipping, returns, sizing, and warranty so it never guesses.

instructions.title: Write tight custom instructions
instructions.body: Use the Behavior tab to set brand voice and dos/don'ts. Keep it short — it is added to every turn.

model.title: Start with a balanced model
model.body: Lower temperature keeps answers focused. Raise the model size only if you need deeper reasoning, since it costs more per reply.

recs.title: Tune recommendation count
recs.body: Show 3–4 products per reply. Too many overwhelms shoppers; too few limits choice.

key.title: Protect your API key
key.body: The OpenAI key lives only in your server environment. Never paste it into the storefront or share it publicly.

channelConnections.title: Meta API connections
channelConnections.webhookUrlNotPublic: Meta only accepts a public HTTPS callback. Open this page on your live domain — or a tunnel — before registering it.

whatsapp.app: Create a Meta app and add the WhatsApp product to it.
whatsapp.config: Create a Facebook Login for Business configuration granting these permissions, and put its ID in META_WHATSAPP_CONFIGURATION_ID.
whatsapp.oauth: In that configuration's settings, add this site's domain to Allowed Domains for the JavaScript SDK and this page's full URL to Valid OAuth Redirect URIs.
whatsapp.webhook: Under Webhooks, register the callback URL shown on this page with your META_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN and subscribe these fields.
whatsapp.connect: Use Continue with Facebook, or fill in the account IDs and access token in the form on this page.
whatsapp.caution: Meta requires business verification and a registered phone number before anyone outside your app's test users can message you.

messenger.app: Add the Messenger product to the same Meta app and connect the Facebook Page you administer.
messenger.permissions: Request these permissions for the Page token.
messenger.webhook: Under Webhooks, register the callback URL shown on this page with your META_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN and subscribe these fields.
messenger.token: Generate a Page access token and enter it in the form on this page together with the Page ID.
messenger.caution: Turn on Human Agent replies only after Meta grants that permission. It is for manual support, never for automated or promotional messages.

instagram.professional: Switch the Instagram account to a professional account (Business or Creator).
instagram.page: Link it to a Facebook Page you administer — Instagram Direct is reached through that Page, so this is required.
instagram.allowAccess: In the Instagram app, turn on Settings → Messages and story replies → Connected tools → Allow access to messages.
instagram.permissions: Add the Instagram product to the same Meta app and request these permissions.
instagram.webhook: Under Webhooks, register the callback URL shown on this page with your META_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN and subscribe these fields.
instagram.connect: Use Continue with Facebook, or fill in the Instagram account ID and the linked Page's access token in the form on this page.
instagram.caution: META_INSTAGRAM_CONFIGURATION_ID must be a Facebook Login for Business configuration. The ID under Instagram → API setup with Instagram login belongs to a different product, and its codes fail the exchange with a redirect_uri error.

telegram.token: Copy the token it replies with and enter it in the Bot token field.
telegram.connect: Connect. Storify registers the webhook itself, so there is nothing to paste into a dashboard.
telegram.share: Share the bot's t.me link so customers can start a conversation.
telegram.caution: Telegram needs no app review and has no reply window — a bot may answer any chat that has started it, at any time.
